title: Deep Learning-embedded 4D-STEM CBED Approach for Mapping Polymorphic Phase Distribution of Doped Hafnia Thin Films
content: Deep learning (DL)-assisted analysis of electron microscopy datasets has emerged as a transformative tool for automated interpretation and high-fidelity signal enhancement in nanomaterials research [1]. Recent advancements integrating DL with four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) have opened promising avenues for correlating crystal symmetries and orientations with nanograin distributions [2]. This capability is critical for resolving complex structural challenges in polycrystalline thin films, particularly in systems such as hafnium zirconium oxide (Hf0.5Zr0.5O2, HZO) ultra-thin films, which are expected to play a pivotal role as ferroelectric switching components in next-generation ultrathin field effect transistors [3-5].
